_about: One entry per attribute shown in the report. dir: lower = lower is better, higher = higher is better, target = should equal `target`, info = context only. goal says what we are trying to achieve; how says how it is computed. build-report.mjs computes the values, the page only renders this catalog. Quality is a gate, cost is the outcome: costToGate, gateMet and their companions are in the group 'gate'; test counts are cost drivers (info).

groups.label: Quality gate: the same quality, and what it cost
Commits: size, logic and the work between them

metrics.label: Mutation score, frontend (adjusted)
metrics.goal: As the backend row. Gate criterion.
metrics.how: mutation.scoreAdjusted, else the raw score (noted).

metrics.label: Mutation score, backend (adjusted)
metrics.goal: Killed plus survivors justified as equivalent, over all mutants, full suite and the project's scope. Gate criterion. Compare only above the threshold as a tie-breaker.
metrics.how: mutation.scoreAdjusted, else the raw score (noted).

metrics.label: Tests added after the first mutation run
metrics.goal: The iteration share of the test count: tests written only to reach the gate after measuring.
metrics.how: Final passing tests minus the tests at the first mutation run (codeMetrics.gate.testsAtFirstMutation).

metrics.label: Mutation survivor rounds
metrics.goal: How often the first full mutation run was not enough. 0 = the tests written before measuring already met the gate. Exposes first-pass luck.
metrics.how: Sum of codeMetrics.gate.mutationRounds over the components.

metrics.label: Gate overshoot (points)
metrics.goal: Quality above the threshold is not needed and cost money. Average points above the threshold over the criteria that passed. Lower means the run stopped at the gate.
metrics.how: Mean of value minus threshold over passed coverage and mutation criteria.

metrics.label: Gate shortfall (points)
metrics.goal: How far the run is below the thresholds, summed over the coverage and mutation criteria it missed. Target: zero.
metrics.how: Sum of threshold minus value for each missed criterion.

metrics.label: Quality gate met
metrics.goal: All runs of a setup must reach the same quality: line coverage and adjusted mutation score at or above the thresholds per component, final run green, no open Critical or High finding. A run that misses it is not comparable.
metrics.how: Computed from the run's coverage, adjusted mutation score, final run and open findings against the thresholds of quality-requirements.md (history: the thresholds set in the config, applied afterwards).

metrics.label: Cost to reach the gate ($)
metrics.goal: The objective. What the run cost, human waiting excluded, to deliver a result that meets the quality gate. Shown only when the gate was met: a run below the gate did not deliver the same quality and cannot be compared.
metrics.how: Cost excl. waits, only when every gate criterion that could be assessed passed.

metrics.label: Agent time
metrics.goal: What the workflow itself needs in minutes, with every wait for a human removed. The main time figure.
metrics.how: Sum over phases of phase wall time minus recorded waits and idle gaps above 10 minutes. Gaps between phases are dropped.

metrics.label: Human wait (excluded)
metrics.goal: Not a property of the workflow but of how the run was operated. Lower means fewer blockers. It is removed from every other number.
metrics.how: Recorded humanInterventions plus idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript, inside phases.

metrics.label: Waits over 1 hour
metrics.goal: Each one lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire and costs a full-context rewrite. Target: none.
metrics.how: Waits longer than 60 minutes, including gaps between phases.

metrics.label: Model time
metrics.goal: Time the model spends generating. It falls with fewer, shorter calls.
metrics.how: Transcript gaps that end in an assistant message (needs the transcript).

metrics.label: Tool time
metrics.goal: Time in builds, test runs and scanners. Shows what to speed up, parallelise or run less often.
metrics.how: Transcript gaps that end in a tool result, without questions to the human (needs the transcript).

metrics.label: Overhead phases (0, 1, 2, 7)
metrics.goal: Preflight, requirements, design and release. Setup work that does not build or test the product; lower is better.
metrics.how: Agent minutes in phases 0, 1, 2 and 7.

metrics.label: Build, test, verify (4 to 6)
metrics.goal: Where the product is made and checked. More here can mean more quality (see mutation score), so it is context, not a target.
metrics.how: Agent minutes in phases 4, 5 and 6.

metrics.label: Agent minutes per passing test
metrics.goal: Not a goal: dividing by the test count would reward writing more tests. Shown for context only.
metrics.how: Agent time divided by the final passing test count.

metrics.label: Cost excl. waits
metrics.goal: Dollars at list prices without the cache rebuilds that waits caused. The comparison figure for cost.
metrics.how: Tokens times list prices, minus the extra of each cache write above 150k tokens that followed a wait over an hour.

metrics.label: Cost as logged
metrics.goal: What the run actually cost. Higher than the line above only when waits caused cache rebuilds.
metrics.how: Tokens times list prices (usage.costUsd); the run-log's own figure where no transcript exists.

metrics.label: Cache rebuilds caused by waits
metrics.goal: Money lost to idling past the cache lifetime. Target: zero.
metrics.how: Cost as logged minus cost excl. waits. Estimated from excess cache-write tokens where no transcript exists.

metrics.label: Cost per passing test
metrics.goal: Not a goal: dividing by the test count would reward writing more tests. Shown for context only.
metrics.how: Cost excl. waits divided by the final passing test count.

metrics.label: Model calls
metrics.goal: Every call re-reads the whole context, so fewer calls is the surest way to lower cost.
metrics.how: Distinct assistant messages in the transcript.

metrics.label: Tool calls
metrics.goal: Fewer, larger steps cost less. Many Edit calls point to rework.
metrics.how: Tool-use entries in the transcript (or the count in the log).

metrics.label: Tool calls that failed
metrics.goal: Failed calls are wasted calls and context.
metrics.how: Tool results with is_error divided by tool calls.

metrics.label: Output tokens
metrics.goal: What the model wrote, including thinking. Output costs five times the price of uncached input.
metrics.how: Sum over calls.

metrics.label: Average context per call
metrics.goal: The main cost driver: each call re-reads all of it at cache-read price. Starting a fresh context per phase lowers it.
metrics.how: Input plus cache read plus cache write tokens per call, averaged.

metrics.label: Peak context
metrics.goal: How large the context got before the end.
metrics.how: Largest context of any call.

metrics.label: Calls above 150k context
metrics.goal: Long contexts are expensive; this is the share of calls in that range.
metrics.how: Calls with more than 150k context tokens divided by all calls.

metrics.label: Blocking decisions
metrics.goal: Each one stops the run for a human. Answers that recur across runs can be given in advance in the inputs.
metrics.how: Decision records of type blocking.

metrics.label: Human interventions
metrics.goal: How often the human had to act or answer.
metrics.how: Entries in humanInterventions.

metrics.label: Approval prompts
metrics.goal: How often the human had to approve a tool call; everything else was decided by the permission mode or the classifier.
metrics.how: Permission decisions in the transcript whose source is not the configuration.

metrics.label: Decision records
metrics.goal: All decisions, blocking or not. A high count with few blocking ones means the agent decides well on its own.
metrics.how: Entries in decisions.

metrics.label: Fix loops
metrics.goal: Rework found in verification. The count alone says little: the same work done earlier shows up as time instead.
metrics.how: Entries in fixLoops.

metrics.label: Fix loop minutes
metrics.goal: What rework actually cost in time. Short loops that fix template-avoidable defects are cheap but still avoidable.
metrics.how: Sum of end minus start over fix loops that record both.

metrics.label: Fix loops that needed a human
metrics.goal: A loop that waits for a human is the expensive kind. Target: none.
metrics.how: fixLoops with needsHuman true (schema 2 logs only).

metrics.label: Frozen-test changes
metrics.goal: Each change to a frozen acceptance test needed a human. Fewer means better requirements and test design.
metrics.how: acceptanceCriteria.frozenTestChanges, or the decisions that approved a manifest change.

metrics.label: Deviations from the process
metrics.goal: Every departure from the rules makes the run less comparable. Target: none.
metrics.how: Entries in divergences (blank when the log has no such field).

metrics.label: Passing tests (final run)
metrics.goal: A cost driver, not a quality measure: the number of tests the run needed to reach the quality gate. More tests are not better and fewer are not better; compare quality by the gate and cost by the cost rows.
metrics.how: finalTestRun.passed, all levels.

metrics.label: Failing tests (final run)
metrics.goal: The run must end green.
metrics.how: finalTestRun.failed.

metrics.label: Failing tests (first run)
metrics.goal: Defects that reached the first full run. Lower means the build phase was cleaner.
metrics.how: firstTestRun.failed (a run that did not compile is blank).

metrics.label: Findings as found
metrics.goal: Issues the verification phase had to deal with.
metrics.how: Sum of findings by severity.

metrics.label: Critical and High as found
metrics.goal: The serious ones. Some are false positives, so read them with the findings table.
metrics.how: findings.critical + findings.high.

metrics.label: Critical and High open at end
metrics.goal: The run may not finish with one open.
metrics.how: openAtEnd.critical + openAtEnd.high (blank when not recorded).

metrics.label: Mutation score, backend (raw)
metrics.goal: Killed mutants over all mutants, with the project's scope. Context: the gate uses the adjusted score. Comparable only for the same scope (see notes).
metrics.how: From codeMetrics or the run summary, with scope.

metrics.label: Mutation score, frontend (raw)
metrics.goal: Killed mutants over all mutants, with the project's scope. Context: the gate uses the adjusted score. Comparable only for the same scope (see notes).
metrics.how: From codeMetrics or the run summary.

metrics.label: Line coverage, backend
metrics.goal: Share of backend code the tests run, all levels together. Part of the quality gate.
metrics.how: From codeMetrics or the run summary.

metrics.label: Line coverage, frontend
metrics.goal: Share of frontend code the tests run, all levels together. Part of the quality gate.
metrics.how: From codeMetrics or the run summary.

metrics.label: Commits
metrics.goal: How the work was cut into steps. Compare with the units in phases.md: about one commit per story, document, layer or fix.
metrics.how: Commits between the start and final commit of the run (git log).

metrics.label: Changed lines per commit (median)
metrics.goal: Typical step size. The guide is small, finished steps: well below 400. A median of 1 to 5 means noise, a median near 400 means batching.
metrics.how: Added plus deleted lines, without logs, lock files and generated or build folders.

metrics.label: Largest commit (changed lines)
metrics.goal: The commit that hurts review most. The guide allows about 400 changed lines or 15 files.
metrics.how: Largest commit by changed lines, same counting as above.

metrics.label: Commits over the size guide
metrics.goal: Share of commits above 15 files or 400 changed lines (working-rules.md). Target: none without a stated reason.
metrics.how: Commits over the guide divided by all commits.

metrics.label: Commits that mix concerns
metrics.goal: Code, tests, documents and build or dependency changes belong in separate commits (working-rules.md). Target: none.
metrics.how: Commits whose changed files fall into more than one of code, test, docs, build.

metrics.label: Commits with a correct message
metrics.goal: Format `<type>: <summary> (IDs)` with a known type and at most 72 characters. Target: 100.
metrics.how: Subjects that match the format divided by all commits.

metrics.label: Commits made within a minute of the previous one
metrics.goal: Several commits created in one burst usually mean work was batched and committed together, not committed when finished. Lower is better.
metrics.how: Commits less than 60 seconds after the previous commit.

metrics.label: Cost between commits (median)
metrics.goal: How much model work piles up before a commit. Small steady steps are cheaper to review and to undo; 0 means the commit came in a burst.
metrics.how: Cost of the model calls between the previous commit and this one (needs the transcript).

metrics.label: Minutes between commits (median, waits removed)
metrics.goal: Rhythm of the work. Very long gaps mean big batches, near zero means bursts.
metrics.how: Time since the previous commit minus waits for a human.

metrics.label: Cost per 100 committed lines
metrics.goal: Cost efficiency of the code and documents that reach the repository.
metrics.how: Cost between commits divided by committed lines, times 100.

metrics.label: Cost of sub-agents
metrics.goal: Work done by sub-agents. Included in the cost above; shown so it is not a surprise.
metrics.how: Calls found in the sub-agent transcripts that sit next to the session file.

metrics.label: Phase timestamps written with the clock tool
metrics.goal: Phase boundaries written by tools/stat.mjs carry the real time; typed ones can be estimates. Target: 100.
metrics.how: Boundaries in run-log.json that match a stat.mjs call in the transcript, within two minutes.

metrics.label: Idle time missing from the log
metrics.goal: Waiting found in the transcript that humanInterventions does not record. Target: none.
metrics.how: Transcript gaps above 10 minutes not covered by a recorded intervention.

metrics.label: Acceptance criteria
metrics.goal: How much behaviour was specified. Context for test counts.
metrics.how: acceptanceCriteria.total or the criteria document.

metrics.label: Production lines
metrics.goal: Size of the product. Cost and time should scale with it, not with process overhead.
metrics.how: cloc, backend plus frontend.

metrics.label: Test lines
metrics.goal: Size of the test code. A cost driver, not a quality measure.
metrics.how: cloc, backend plus frontend.

metrics.label: Test to production lines
metrics.goal: Test lines per production line. A cost driver, not a quality measure.
metrics.how: Test lines divided by production lines.

metrics.label: Tests per 1000 production lines
metrics.goal: Size of the suite relative to the product, a cost driver.
metrics.how: Final passing tests divided by production lines, times 1000.

metrics.label: Unit tests (final run)
metrics.goal: Unit tests needed to reach the gate. Acceptance and end-to-end tests are fixed by the inputs.
metrics.how: finalTestRun.byLevel.unit.

metrics.label: End-to-end tests (final run)
metrics.goal: Fixed by the scenario list of the inputs; a different number means the scenarios were split or added.
metrics.how: finalTestRun.byLevel.e2e.
